question: A loss of 12% gets converted into a profit of 8.5% when the selling price of an article is increased by ₹164. The cost price of article is:
solution:
**Given:**

Loss = 12%

Profit = 8.5%

Difference in profit % and loss % = 164

**Formula used:**

Selling price = Cost price + (Cost price × profit%)

Selling price = Cost price - (Cost price × loss%)

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price be 100x

Selling price of 1st case = 100x - 100x × 12%

⇒100x - (100 × 12/100) = 88x

Selling price of 2nd case = 100x + 100x × 8.5%

⇒ 100x + (100x × 8.5/100) = 108.5x

According to the question,

108.5x - 88x = 164

⇒ 20.5x = 164

⇒ x = (164/20.5)

⇒ x = 8

So, the cost price of the article = 100 × 8 = Rs. 800

**∴ The cost price of the article is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let CP = 100 units

According to the question

108% of CP - 88% of CP = 164

⇒ 108.5 units - 88 units = Rs. 164

⇒ 20.5 units = Rs. 164

⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 8

∴ CP = 100 × 8 = Rs.800

Hence, The cost price of the article is ₹800.
